Since there is a significant gap between L (NFA)/? and L (NFA)/poly, it might be beneficial to investigate the impact of advice size to the power of non-determinism in a more fine-grained way. In particular, we have shown that linear advice is sufficient for NFA to recognize languages outside of L (PFA)/?, and cubic advice is sufficient for PFA to recognize languages outside of L (NFA)/poly. It would be interesting to know where are the precise boundaries when L (PFA)/f (n) 6⊆ L (NFA)/g(n) and vice-versa. Also, our results hold for one-way automata. We expect that the situation for two-way automata would be significantly different. Since the relation of one-way versus two-way is in general important, we believe it would be beneficial to investigate it also in the non-uniform case.
